comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SESSION 2026-08-06/07 — orphan triage, bridge-redesign planning, and a large parallel remediation round.

STARTED AS: list open epics with child counts, plus open bugs/tasks/stories with no parent. Grew into a full remediation session.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
* Orphan tickets (open, parentless bug/task/story): 75 -> 44.
* ~48 commits landed on origin/main.
* Tickets closed this session: 192e, 3787, c08d, ab79, two jira probes, 2a76, 8de5, ed5e, 3bdf, 5dd2, e5ec, 39c5, 83f2, 3b92, 46a2, e6a0, 0ba2, 354d, 78f4, 0ee6, c494, d166, 7c58, e548, a5f5, d5ae, dbb2, a371, 4c2b, 4bf4, 2be7, 851e, 65d7, ccf6, 13b4, 599e, 63e8, e7a9, 6067, 24f7.

EPIC 2f79 (bridge redesign) — PLANNED AND SPLIT
* Was 9 children with ZERO dependency edges and ZERO declared file impact. Now: file impact on all children, 15+ dependency edges, acyclic, two roots.
* 4752 would not converge under plan review (findings went 2 -> 7 -> 4 -> 7) because it bundled three verb retirements, a flag removal, three renames, a new verb and a production workflow rewiring. SPLIT into: 4752 (verb group, rescoped), c61a (retire dead verbs), 4a44 (retire reconcile + --mode), e27c (rename survivors).
* 1c1b CERTIFIED (plan-review PASS) after six rounds; findings fell 3->3->2->1->2->0.
* Review found real defects, not presentation: push.py would have pushed NOTHING after the YAML deletion (no staging/commit); a SECOND undiscovered CAS loop in the canary workflow; 1c1b depending on the BRIDGE_ALERT emitter that 030f deletes; reconcile/--mode living on THREE surfaces while the plan enumerated one.

OPERATOR DECISIONS RECORDED
* e7a9: REFUSE secret-bearing writes, with an allowed force override. Redaction rejected. IMPLEMENTED AND MERGED (33d6d4ef7c).
* 2876: direct-Anthropic arm IS approved as a fallback.
* 24f7: clean break, no alias. MERGED.
* 5e53: module-size remediation DEFERRED.
* 858c: an unmeetable AC is a defect in the AC, remediate before close — BUT genuinely N/A for a won't-fix/obsolete disposition. Reopened and rescoped to a disposition-keyed mechanism keyed off --class.
* 63e8: advisories block the SCHEDULED main run and RELEASES; Gerrit verify blocks only when the change touches the dependency map ('if you touch it, you own it'). Severity bar CRITICAL/HIGH fail, MEDIUM warn, LOW track; UNRATED treated as HIGH. override-dependencies approved as a documented escape hatch. MERGED (0767c38ebb).
* 9fb3: DROP inspect-ai (option A) — it is never imported yet is the sole cause of both [tool.uv] conflicts entries AND the click override behind PYSEC-2026-2132. IN FLIGHT.
* 556a: option E — do NOT move inbound_fields.py; rewrite the exemption to state it is the deliberate price of the J7 adapter seal.
* 81d5: option B — anti-drift guard, not the glob. AC3 needs rewording.
* 8fbd-e9d5: fallback chain stays OFF and the fix is COMMITTED TO (not deferred) — capability intersection silently downgrades every standard-class call project-wide.
* 7084: R5 (name the lock holder, using EXISTING stamp machinery) + R1 (batch the introducing-commit resolution) + R3 (lock-polite compact-on-close; load is intermittent so no skip-floor needed) APPROVED. R2/R4/R6 declined. Per-ticket locking recorded as a FUTURE consideration if round 1 underdelivers.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPEN STATE AT HANDOFF (2026-08-07)

IN FLIGHT (3 subagents)
* 7084 R1+R3+R5 — the lock-duration remediation. Two/three separate Gerrit changes.
* 9fb3 — dropping inspect-ai, which should also remove both [tool.uv] conflicts entries and the click override.
* 9f63 — /rebar-debug on the review-bot trigger defect.

AWAITING SOMEONE TO PRESS SUBMIT
* Gerrit 1463 ('Bank verifier AC verdicts; scale floor; read memo') and 1477 ('a9dd: prefetch file_impact into verifier context') have BOTH gates green and have sat unsubmitted for hours. Not owned by this session.

TICKETS LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY, WITH REASONS
* 514d-a8d8 — genuinely NOT resolved. An earlier triage called it RESOLVED and that was wrong: the ticket targets the CODE-REVIEW CloudWatch totals but commit bf9fb62a6f only wired the PLAN-REVIEW path. code_review/batch_runner.py has zero 'usage' occurrences and finalize.py:139-141 still documents the gap in the present tense.
* 7084 — open pending R1/R3/R5 results; per-ticket locking is the round-2 option if they underdeliver.
* 858c — reopened and rescoped to a disposition-keyed N/A mechanism.
* 2876 — open: AC1 done, AC2 n/a, AC3 half (resolution fixed; preflight blocked on the credential below), AC4 not implemented.
* 535e (NEW, status=idea) — treat the compaction SNAPSHOT as a derived cache and regenerate on conflict. Carries the full prior-art research.

SYSTEMIC FINDINGS WORTH THEIR OWN ATTENTION
* 9f63 — the LLM-Review bot silently skips patch-set uploads. FOUR reproductions across three agents. The signature rules out a slow queue: newer changes OVERTOOK one stalled 70 minutes, and the bot voted 3 minutes after a manual nudge. Two different nudges revive it (recheck-review comment, or a no-op rebase), suggesting the review queues on an event the upload failed to emit. It caused an agent to abandon finished, correct work believing the bot was down.
* 7084 — measured: a ticket close held the store write lock 48.1s, of which 47.77s (99.2%) was _build_authorship_ledger running ONE git log --full-history PER SIGNED EVENT (6.78s each) while the actual mutation took 0.4s. Worst case measured 488s. Contention repro: one long holder + 6 concurrent comments = 6/6 failed at 60s and ALL SIX WRITES WERE PERMANENTLY LOST.
* ab54 — a live orphaned uncommitted COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar was observed (benign here, a tracked duplicate existed). Suggested an fsck-style check for on-disk-but-untracked event files.
* d2df — the runaway completion verifier STILL reproduces on current main; updating did NOT fix it. It clusters on tickets whose criteria have no single source anchor (test-infrastructure tickets), pointing at context pre-selection rather than the guard.
* 599e-class 'guarantees that are not mechanically enforced': an entire test surface (38 tests across 11 files) passed by NOT RUNNING because no CI lane installed the reviewbot/ui extras; and 24f7's tree-wide check was a MANUAL grep, not a committed test — which is exactly why 63e8 reintroduced the retired --force-close spelling in a new file minutes after 24f7 retired it. General lesson recorded: a grep sweep is only valid as of the sha it ran against.
* CI capacity, not review or agent throughput, was the binding constraint for the last third of the session (9 runs queued deep).

OPERATOR ACTION STILL NEEDED
* ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: a VALID key exists in ~/.zshrc (HTTP 200) but a DIFFERENT, INVALID key (HTTP 401) shadows it in the non-interactive environment agents and gates run in. Same length, different hash. NOT from ~/.zshenv/.zprofile/.profile (zero references) — injected upstream. Consequence: every provider measurement taken against the direct-Anthropic arm in a non-interactive context measured an invalid credential, contaminating evidence on 1e88 and 2391.

PROCESS LESSONS FOR THE NEXT SESSION
* A 'completed' agent notification is NOT proof the agent stopped — it fires whenever an agent has no live children, and one resumed after mine. Never point a second agent at an existing worktree; that caused a real collision on e7a9.
* Backgrounded 'sleep' returns immediately; it does not wait. Two agents lost time to this.
* After a rebase or conflict resolution, re-run the FULL gate, not just tests — a one-blank-line lint slip cost a full CI cycle in a saturated queue.

LATE ADDITION — ticket-state drift observed during the closing verification sweep.

858c read back as 'closed' despite having been reopened and re-verified earlier, with its rescoped description and both comments fully intact. The DESCRIPTION write survived; only the STATUS was reverted. Re-reopened and re-verified as open.

That asymmetry matters for diagnosis: it is a status-only overwrite, not a revision rollback, which points at inbound field-level reconciliation rather than an event-log or compaction fault. Jira still held the ticket closed from the earlier (superseded) close, and the Reconcile Bridge was re-enabled mid-session. Another agent independently reported 556a drifting open -> in_progress in the same window. Evidence recorded on 4136.

VERIFICATION SWEEP RESULT: all other tickets touched this session read back in their intended states — 16 spot-checked closures all closed; 7084 in_progress with 11 comments; 2876/81d5/556a/8fbd/514d open with their decision comments; 9fb3 and 9f63 in_progress with their agents; 535e created as status=idea and linked discovered_from 7084. Session log is this ticket (f218-d02e-e4be-400d), two entries.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LATE FINDINGS (2026-08-07, after the verification sweep)

7084 LOCK WORK LANDED — R5 (1507), R1 (1508), R3 (1510), all merged with both gates green. R1 measured on a 71,041-commit clone: 4-file ticket 29.81s->1.05s (28x); 25 files 193.16s->4.72s (41x); 73 files 546.00s->4.27s (128x); 155 files 1165.54s->2.09s (557x); zero mismatches across 257 events. The material change is that the AFTER column does not grow with event count — cost is now per-compaction, not per-event, so the unbounded growth is gone. Equivalence proven four ways including an explicit off-first-parent fixture (same event added on both sides of a merge, so the merge is TREESAME to both parents; the test asserts the simplified query returns something DIFFERENT, so the fixture cannot silently stop exercising the case). 7084 left in_progress: R3's floor question, the terminal-and-lossy acquire budget, and post-R1 re-measurement under the 6-writer harness are all still open.

858c STATUS REVERSION — ROOT-CAUSED, NOT A REGRESSION FROM THIS SESSION. Inbound wrote a real newer STATUS event authored by 'reconciler'; the reducer was never wrong. Mechanism: _advance_baselines advances from the PASS-START snapshot taken before the outbound apply, so in the pass where rebar pushes a status the baseline keeps the OLD value. A reopen is a revert to a previous value and lands exactly in that window: local 'open' equals the stale baseline, outbound suppresses, inbound then mirrors Jira's stale 'closed' back. Description survived because it DIFFERED from the stale baseline and was pushed; status was clobbered because it EQUALLED it. Timing is decisive: the clobbering pass ran 10:14:54Z, every suspect commit landed 12:16Z-13:13Z. Identical shape found on 2026-07-20 across 8 tickets, 18 days earlier. Self-limiting (baseline advances after a clobber, next pass pushes local out) so no bridge pause needed. Filed as e6e9-ddbf-223b-4f49 (P1). AWAITING OPERATOR DECISION between fix A (advance the baseline to what was actually pushed) and fix B (state fields never lose to inbound).

COVERAGE GAP behind it: ADR 0026 mandates a direction-preservation cell and it exists for 'title' ONLY. The status equivalent drives adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields, which has NO PRODUCTION CALLER — status has never been pinned on the live path.

THIRD INSTANCE of the same class today: 599e (38 tests across 11 files passing by NOT RUNNING), 24f7 (a tree-wide check that was a manual grep, not a committed test), and now a test exercising a function nothing calls. All three looked like coverage and were not.

SECOND REGRESSION FROM 0767c38ebb (63e8) reaching main within hours: canary_bridge.py:31 does a bare 'import alert_dedup' that resolves only when scripts/ is on sys.path, so subset test runs error (2 errors, CI's full run green). Filed as 291e-7b48-3f24-41c6, linked discovered_from 63e8. Same defect class as a371, whose guard covers 'tests.'-rooted imports under tests/ but NOT bare imports of scripts/ modules — the class is half-guarded.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FINAL ENTRY (2026-08-07, session close)

WORK COMPLETED SINCE THE HANDOFF ENTRY

* 7084 CLOSED. R1/R3/R5 merged (Gerrit 1507/1508/1510). R1 measured 28x-557x on the real 71k-commit store; the 155-file ticket went 1165.54s -> 2.09s, and the after-column no longer grows with event count, so the unbounded growth is gone. Acceptance criteria were REMEDIATED rather than force-ticked: original AC1 described R2 (hoist the ledger out of the lock), which was declined because at ~1s there is no reason to accept its race; original AC2 asked for a worktree field the operator's existing-machinery scope for R5 excludes.
* 9fb3 CLOSED, merged bcd77a8eaf. Dropping the unused inspect-ai dependency also removed BOTH [tool.uv] conflicts entries and the click override, each proved unnecessary by re-running the resolver rather than assumed: uv sync --locked --extra dev --extra bedrock now INSTALLS (the pair the fork forbade), the lock reaches click 8.4.2 unaided, pip-audit clean. Lock diff was pure removal, 46 packages dropped, zero version changes to anything retained. The [eval] extra was removed entirely.
* e6e9 CLOSED, merged a55b93a0f5. Option A implemented with real per-mutation success plumbing, not an approximation of the pass exit code. Deliberately all-or-nothing per update_issue call, on the reasoning that under-reporting makes the baseline LAG (next pass re-pushes) while over-reporting makes it LEAD, which never self-corrects. RED proof by neutering the fix to pre-fix behaviour: 7 failed / 9 passed, with the held-firm and soft-fail cells staying GREEN through the neutering — proving they pin behaviour the fix must not change. Live-path direction preservation added for all five mirrored fields WITH a runtime reachability assertion, closing the gap where those cells had only ever driven a function with no production caller.
* 24f7 CLOSED with a passing verifier, no force.
* 10c3 FILED (P1): a write whose lock acquire times out is PERMANENTLY LOST. Measured 6/6 concurrent comments lost at 60s. First acceptance criterion is to RE-MEASURE against post-R1 main before building anything — at ~1s holds the timeout may now be unreachable, which would rescope it.
* 3b93 FILED: entering the review-bot app lifespan in a test inherits a 1200s shutdown drain. Prevention only (bound SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS globally in tests + an autouse fixture making the stubbed path default); an AST lint was considered and explicitly rejected as poor-signal. Linked discovered_from 89d5.
* 291e FILED: canary_bridge's bare 'import alert_dedup' resolves only when scripts/ is on sys.path. SECOND regression from 0767c38ebb within hours.
* 89d5 (py3.11 cell) enriched with four occurrences and, importantly, a CORRECTION: the 99%-hang mode is NOT always runner-side. An A/B against clean origin/main @1afdbbd0be proved one instance was a real test defect — 'with TestClient(app)' entering the app lifespan and inheriting a 1200s drain. The two modes are distinguishable from the log (hang = progress percentage, orphaned children, no summary; crash = names the test and the gw worker) and need OPPOSITE responses.

STILL OPEN AT SESSION END
* 9f63 in_progress, Gerrit 1512 at patch set 7 (LLM-Review +1 PASS). Its agent is doing a single recheck; the Verified -1 is the known py3.11 worker-crash, not its change.
* 10c3, 3b93, 291e, 535e (idea), 858c, 2876, 81d5, 556a, 8fbd, 514d — all with decisions or evidence recorded.

TWO PROCESS LESSONS I LEARNED THE HARD WAY THIS SESSION
* Do NOT act on a Gerrit change an agent owns. gerrit-verify.yaml sets cancel-in-progress keyed on the change id, so a stray recheck KILLS the in-flight run and restarts a ~70-minute clock. I did this on 1505 while its agent was managing it. The right move is SendMessage to the owner, which worked well on 1512.
* Never print an unconditional success echo after a store write. Two writes in this session's tail were silently lost to lock timeouts while my echo claimed success; only a follow-up read caught it. Verify by re-reading, always.

R5 CONFIRMED WORKING IN PRODUCTION: a lost write surfaced as 'flock: could not acquire lock after 60s (holder: host=... pid=17905 held=117s pid_state=live)'. The old message said only '60s'. Note held=117s is well above R1's ~1s target — useful evidence for 10c3.
